title: From 15% to 90% GPU Utilization: Fix the Data Pipeline, Not the Model
talk_summary: A multimodal SFT training pipeline was GPU-starved (15% utilization) because data loading, preprocessing, and transport were serial and synchronous. Adding concurrency, prefetching, zero-copy object references, and spread scheduling raised utilization to ~90% and gave 50% extra throughput at scale.

takeaways.technique: Prefetch work ahead of the consumer
takeaways.what_they_do: A background producer fills a queue ahead of the trainer so data is ready on demand instead of fetched when requested.
takeaways.numbers: data fetch/processing per batch dropped to ~0s; wait ratio 85% -> 20%

takeaways.what_they_do: They chose async IO for network fetches and process workers for CPU-bound image work rather than one lever everywhere.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we need to match our bottleneck. Not simply going with a lever that's worked for us before

takeaways.technique: Zero-copy object references instead of passing payloads
takeaways.what_they_do: Samples carry a pointer to a shared object store rather than being pickled/copied between processes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Each sample carries a object reference which is just a pointer to the data
takeaways.numbers: eliminated extraneous put_object calls; comm cost and wait ratio down

takeaways.technique: Spread scheduling to avoid single-node bottleneck
takeaways.what_they_do: Ray colocated workers by default, saturating one NIC; spreading workers across nodes plus zero-copy retrieval fixed it at scale.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's easy to bottleneck one machine before you move to another machine
takeaways.numbers: 50% additional throughput at scale from two flags

takeaways.what_they_do: Flags that showed no benefit small-scale had a synergistic effect at large scale, so they tested at both sizes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: config can do poorly at a small scale but can do really good at a larger scale
takeaways.numbers: neither flag helped small-scale; together +50% at scale

takeaways.technique: Profile the baseline to find the real bottleneck
takeaways.what_they_do: They used flame graphs to discover time was in S3 loads, not the model, before optimizing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: profiling your baseline helps you move the needle
takeaways.numbers: baseline 85% of time on data acquisition
